title: Spillover routing policy: capacity-aware cross-variant & cross-region traffic spill for progressive rollouts
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Design and implement a Spillover Routing Policy that prevents hard outages during progressive rollouts by proactively spilling excess traffic from a primary variant to compatible fallbacks across capacity tiers and regions. The policy should respect model-compatibility hints encoded in model manifests, maintain session-level affinity for A/B/experiment groups, and allow shadowing alongside live spillover. It must integrate with the existing routing layer and the rollout controller so that canary steps, A/B weights, and shadow streams are preserved while avoiding unexpected latency spikes or capacity storms.
comments: 2025-11-10 - Marisol Vega: Initial RFC sketched for spillover routing. Goals: avoid 503s during variant scale-up/scale-down, keep tail latency SLAs, and preserve experiment integrity for A/B tests.

2025-11-12 - Tariq Ahmed: Implementation proposal — extend runtime routing table with spillover chains. Each chain is an ordered list of candidate variants annotated with compatibility score, capacity tier, and regional proximity. Runtime picks first candidate with available admission tokens; if none, apply degrade policy (probabilistic fallback to cached response or delayed enqueue).

2025-11-13 - Elinor Park (PM): Please ensure we surface metrics to Console: spilled_requests, spill_rate_by_variant, average_spill_latency, and per-experiment drift. Also need a confidence signal for auto-rollback triggers that considers spill activity.
2025-11-14 - Security review request sent by Tariq. Need clarification whether variant manifests may contain external URLs for compatibility data (they will not).

2025-11-15 - Infra (J. Rossi): Concern: cross-region spill could double-egress cost if traffic flips regions. Recommend prioritizing same-region fallbacks, then cross-region with explicit project opt-in.
2025-11-16 - Design (S. Liu): UX note — Console should show a visualization of the spill graph for a rollout so on-call can quickly see which variants are absorbing overflow.

2025-11-17 - Tariq Ahmed: Spike results: implemented prototype in feature branch. Basic spill chain applied to canary traffic; synthetic canaries passed but observed 5% increase in p95 for spill paths due to cross-region latency. Next: implement locality-weighted selection and per-route latency budget enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a spillover chain per rollout with ordered fallback candidates and compatibility scores
Spillover selects same-region compatible fallback prior to cross-region candidates when possible
Session affinity maintained for A/B cohorts even when spillover occurs (sticky assignment recorded in rollout metadata)
Console dashboard shows real-time spilled_requests and spill_rate_by_variant; on-call can filter by region and experiment
Auto-rollback logic includes a spill-aware signal to avoid false positives (e.g., transient spill to warm new variant should not immediately rollback unless error/quality regressions are detected)
End-to-end e2e test simulating capacity exhaustion results in zero 5xx for 99% of requests and documented fallbacks for remaining ones
Security review completed and no external reachouts added to model manifests
notes: Key decisions: (1) compatibility hints live in model manifest as a short list of compatible model family tags and a semantic compatibility score (0..100) computed during model onboarding; (2) admission token accounting extended to aggregator-level so spillovers do not starve primary capacity; (3) cross-region spill disabled by default and gated behind project opt-in; (4) auto-rollback receives a normalized spill_signal to avoid noisy rollbacks during controlled warm-up.
implementation_plan: Week1: Extend manifest schema and onboarding pipeline to surface compatibility hints and compatibility score
Week2: Add spill chain data structures to routing layer and implement same-region-first selection algorithm
Week3: Integrate with rollout controller and maintain per-session stickiness metadata
Week4: Instrument metrics, add Console visuals and alerts, run chaos tests that exhaust capacity
Week5: Soft launch on internal projects, collect ops feedback, and iterate before full rollout
